items.title: The units at stage 1: the µeV core kept, the scale fixed by convention, one lever-arm ratio in θ
items.brief: Keep the µeV core and fix the scale by convention: no measurement can pin the absolute scale, so a scale parameter would waste the crowd.

decision.label: lever-arm mean fixed at 0.09
decision.detail: Geometric mean of the two lever arms fixed at 0.09; θ carries their ratio.

decision.label: scale invisible to diagrams
decision.detail: Scaling lever arms and energies together leaves the diagram identical.

decision.label: gate placement unaffected
decision.detail: Placing the gate was measured not to need the absolute scale.

decision.label: both dots treated alike
decision.detail: The geometric mean favours neither dot.

alternatives.label: volt-referred core
alternatives.detail: Zeeman energies are absolute, so a volts-to-µeV factor is needed anyway.

alternatives.label: scale as a parameter
alternatives.detail: The diagram cannot see it; crowd members would spread along it.

alternatives.label: measuring the scale
alternatives.detail: An energy reference was not built; placement does not need it.

assumes.label: nothing pinned in absolute µeV
assumes.detail: Breaks once an outside value is fixed in absolute energy.

assumes.label: detuning constants not fixed
assumes.detail: Charge-noise amplitude inferred; the rest freed or quoted per volt.

assumes.label: barrier terms fit the argument
assumes.detail: Re-check when barrier physics adds its per-volt terms.

consequences.label: outside energies need conversion
consequences.detail: Compare via their own lever arm, or in plunger mV.

consequences.label: brackets in project units
consequences.detail: 1000-2000 µeV charging energy, 4.47 µeV coupling ceiling: not absolute.

consequences.label: input layer builds on it
consequences.detail: Input layer seed formula, θ electrostatics, the lever-arm ratio prior.

context.label: diagrams blind to scale
context.detail: Stage 1 reads gate volts; the core works in µeV.

context.label: 16 scaled twin devices
context.detail: Readings differ 0.03-0.15 sd median, 0.89 sd worst.

context.label: placement barely moves
context.detail: Fidelity landscape differs at most 2.5e-05 across twins.

recheck.label: RIKEN's barrier slope 2.6x shallower
recheck.detail: 0.03 per mV against the prior's 0.08; their lever arm 80-100 brackets our 90.

items.title: The input layer, built: the typical gate three times closer, no failure fixed, and the diagram weakest where it matters
items.brief: Build the input layer: upstream readings become the crowd's starting box. The typical gate lands three times closer, but no failure is fixed.

decision.label: readings to a starting box
decision.detail: Seed formula gives electrostatics, qubit frequencies give Zeeman; errors set a flat box.

decision.label: honest by construction
decision.detail: Over 300 devices, intervals held the truth 99-100% of the time.

decision.label: changes nothing else
decision.detail: Default path and earlier runs reproduce bit for bit.

decision.label: failures lie elsewhere
decision.detail: What it leaves belongs to search and calibration.

alternatives.label: seeding from a network
alternatives.detail: The prior seeds as well at three parameters.

alternatives.label: rewriting the global prior
alternatives.detail: Replaced by per-device boxes carrying the same thing.

alternatives.label: only one input
alternatives.detail: Only both together removed every ordinary-device loss.

assumes.label: ratio without absolute scale
assumes.detail: One interdot coupling seen through both plungers.

assumes.label: upstream gives both frequencies
assumes.detail: Without them the loop infers the Zeeman difference itself.

consequences.label: no failure fixed
consequences.detail: Device 29's alias decides the mean; device 24 loses about 2e-3 unflagged.

consequences.label: weakest on hard devices
consequences.detail: On 24 and 29 the box stays nearly the prior.

consequences.label: no rounds saved
consequences.detail: A better placed gate, not a shorter tune-up.

consequences.label: open question to Cornelius
consequences.detail: What ANITA reports and how precisely, especially triple points.

context.label: scope moved downstream
context.detail: Upstream measurements were to become the starting belief.

context.label: 32 devices, median shortfall
context.detail: 8.2e-05 control, 2.5e-05 with the input layer.

context.label: losses over 1e-3
context.detail: 2 control, 3 with the layer (22, 24, 29).

items.title: The scope: QUAST starts where the lab's tools stop - a device ready for two-qubit work
items.brief: Start QUAST from a device ready for two-qubit work and take it to a placed CZ. ANITA already automates everything before that.

decision.label: the build order
decision.detail: Input layer first, then barrier control; not charge sensing or drive calibration.

decision.label: the unautomated steps
decision.detail: Exchange calibration and the two-qubit gate.

decision.label: earlier steps already done
decision.detail: ANITA, or by hand at RIKEN today.

decision.label: charging energy from diagram
decision.detail: A few per cent; a separate measurement saved nothing.

alternatives.label: start from formed dots
alternatives.detail: ANITA already reaches one charge per dot and calibrates the drive.

alternatives.label: a charge-sensing stage
alternatives.detail: Adds one number already on the lab's diagram.

alternatives.label: from a cold chip
alternatives.detail: Redoes years of the lab's work for little new.

assumes.label: upstream delivers a ready device
assumes.detail: ANITA, or by hand at RIKEN as today.

assumes.label: ANITA works beyond germanium
assumes.detail: Shown once, unpublished, not on silicon or at RIKEN.

consequences.label: narrower automation claim
consequences.detail: From a two-qubit-ready device; cold chip to CZ is joint with ANITA.

consequences.label: depends on upstream
consequences.detail: If ANITA falls short, the shelved builds become the work list.

consequences.label: a hand-off contract
consequences.detail: Every assumption, its source and its fall-back.

context.label: ANITA automates the start
context.detail: Cold chip to calibrated single-qubit gates in about an hour.

context.label: charge sensing adds little
context.detail: Median shortfall 8.2e-05 to 2.8e-05; rounds 3.78 to 3.72.

context.label: device 24 still failing
context.detail: Lost about 1e-3 unflagged even with it.

items.title: Mixed precision on a graphics card: a tune-up in about six seconds, gates as good as double
items.brief: Add an opt-in mixed-precision mode on the graphics card: a tune-up drops from 35-40 s to about six, gates matching double precision.

decision.label: the precision split
decision.detail: Levels and phases in double; propagators, noise, likelihoods in single.

decision.label: level solver from nearest pole
decision.detail: Agrees with the double solver to 7e-12.

decision.label: matches double
decision.detail: To about a millionth; places the same gate.

decision.label: opt-in only
decision.detail: The default stays double on the processor.

alternatives.label: double on the card
alternatives.detail: 0.9 times the processor's speed; gaming cards are slow in double.

alternatives.label: plain single
alternatives.detail: Huge phases overflow to NaN on over half the candidates.

alternatives.label: pure single, new solver
alternatives.detail: A few per cent wrong at crossings, only 1.4 times faster.

alternatives.label: library batched eigensolver
alternatives.detail: Asked for 17 GB; chunked, it took most of a tune-up.

assumes.label: the gate splits into blocks
assumes.detail: The π pulse never mixes the like-spin pair with the rest.

assumes.label: arrowhead shape holds
assumes.detail: Spin-flip tunnelling or a drive during exchange breaks it; code falls back.

assumes.label: one process per card
assumes.detail: Three on the 8 GB card ran out of memory.

consequences.label: about thirty times faster
consequences.detail: Both batteries indistinguishable within run-to-run spread.

consequences.label: noise grid risk untouched
consequences.detail: The bigger scaling risk stays on the v2 list.

consequences.label: barrier control uses it
consequences.detail: Barrier control's tune-ups; runs on Oxford's ARC cluster.

context.label: cards fast only in single
context.detail: Most of a tune-up is simulator linear algebra.

context.label: mixed against double
context.detail: Readings, likelihoods, fidelities within 1.7e-6; same placed gate.

context.label: 32 devices
context.detail: Median shortfall 7.5e-05 against 8.2e-05; 0.1 against 3.2 minutes.

items.title: The placement menu was the largest loss in the system; the gate is now placed continuously, and the guard is back
items.brief: Place the gate continuously, not from a fixed menu: the menu was the system's largest loss, about a hundred times inference's.

decision.label: continuous operating point
decision.detail: Hold time solved from each candidate's own CZ time.

decision.label: guard restored
decision.detail: Guard and second opinion back at the stop decision.

decision.label: menu loss was huge
decision.detail: Mean 1.3e-03; 17 of 32 devices lost over 1e-3.

decision.label: median shortfall 2.3e-05
decision.detail: Down from 1.2e-03, with no more rounds.

alternatives.label: fixed 120-entry menu
alternatives.detail: The largest single loss measured in the system.

alternatives.label: dense 64 x 800 grid
alternatives.detail: Continuous matches or beats it on 8 of 8, in 0.1-0.3 s.

alternatives.label: lean loop, no guard
alternatives.detail: Unflagged alias losses: device 29 by 0.042, device 20 by 1.8e-03.

assumes.label: hold set by the phase
assumes.detail: Phase at π fixes it; seeding with each CZ time keeps the peak.

assumes.label: the guard's standard
assumes.detail: No unflagged loss above 1e-3 on 32 devices.

consequences.label: the guard is expensive
consequences.detail: 9.0 against 2.6 minutes a device.

consequences.label: earlier fidelities understated
consequences.detail: They were measured against the menu's cap.

consequences.label: operating point becomes vector
consequences.detail: At barrier control the barrier joins the detuning.

context.label: menu holds 34% apart
context.detail: A CZ needs its phase at π.

context.label: lost to the menu
context.detail: Mean 1.3e-03, worst 6.4e-03 on device 24.

context.label: guard dropped again
context.detail: Missed device 29's alias, so dropped on 30 Sept.

items.title: The loop cleaned up: the guard and the second opinion retired, knowingly
items.brief: Retire the guard and second opinion: runs were about four times slower, and the fit check flagged every wrong gate the lean loop placed.

decision.label: fit check and redo stay
decision.detail: Fit check, exact redo, two rounds before stopping, stopping rule, phase ladder.

decision.label: small cost on hard devices
decision.detail: Failures 1 in 12 to 3; ordinary devices no different.

decision.label: every failure flagged
decision.detail: Misfit z of 124, 72, 94 against 5.

decision.label: fix at barrier control
decision.detail: Detuning-only tuning would not carry over.

alternatives.label: keep the guard
alternatives.detail: Saved 24 and 29 but cost up to 149 s a device.

alternatives.label: narrow-region search now
alternatives.detail: Deferred to barrier control, tested on the hard battery.

assumes.label: wrong-device crowds flagged
assumes.detail: A crowd on a wrong device fails the fit check.

assumes.label: ordinary devices like hard ones
assumes.detail: Broke next day: aliases passed the check on 32 devices.

consequences.label: flagged wrong gates
consequences.detail: About three runs in twelve on the hardest devices.

consequences.label: lost crowds not re-searched
consequences.detail: Flagged, but not searched again.

consequences.label: the hard-device battery
consequences.detail: The test barrier control's redesigned search must pass.

context.label: four times slower
context.detail: Did they still change any gate?

context.label: switched off on same runs
context.detail: Over 1e-3: 1 of 12 with, 3 of 12 without.

context.label: slow at the stop decision
context.detail: Mean 51 s against 12 s, worst 149 s.

items.title: The crowd drives the loop: 44 times closer to the best gate, every earlier failure fixed
items.brief: Let the crowd drive the loop instead of the network: it came 44 times closer to the best gate and fixed every earlier failure.

decision.label: the crowd's role
decision.detail: Carries over rounds, chooses measurements, places the gate on the corrected surrogate.

decision.label: the network's role
decision.detail: Seeds round one, sets the agreement rule, is the fall-back.

decision.label: earlier failures fixed
decision.detail: Devices 29, 24, 17, 7 and 14 all placed the best gate.

decision.label: network overconfident
decision.detail: The crowd corrected to exact is calibrated.

alternatives.label: the network driving
alternatives.detail: 90% intervals held about 50%; lost over 1e-3 on 13 of 32.

alternatives.label: the crowd as first tried
alternatives.detail: Catastrophic on four aliased devices; stopped after one round.

alternatives.label: card simulator in double
alternatives.detail: No faster; single overflowed.

assumes.label: rounds are cheap
assumes.detail: Priced at 5 s of thinking a round.

consequences.label: three times the wall clock
consequences.detail: 66 against 23 minutes; 8-17 minutes a device.

consequences.label: network not needed
consequences.detail: A crowd from the prior proved as good; no v2 retrain.

consequences.label: every later loop builds on it
consequences.detail: Every later loop and the v2 design.

context.label: aliased devices rerun
context.detail: Crowd had been catastrophic on four; rerun on all 32.

context.label: crowd shortfall 44x smaller
context.detail: 3.1e-03 network against 7.1e-05 crowd.

context.label: better on 18 of 32
context.detail: Better on 18, same on 12, worse on 2.
